reason: Broken on the locator. The wording is right; the chapter is not. I obtained a full text of the Beacon Press edition of the Mobi Ho translation (a 7.7 MB scanned-and-OCRed PDF, extracted with pdftotext to 190,474 characters) and read the front matter and the passage. Title page: 'The Miracle of Mindfulness: An Introduction to the Practice of Meditation, Translated by Mobi Ho, With Eleven Drawings by Vo-Dinh Mai, Beacon Press Boston'; copyright page: '(c) 1975, 1976 by Thich Nhat Hanh / Preface and English translation (c) 1975, 1976, 1987 by Mobi Ho', 'Translation of Phep la cua su tinh thuc'. The Contents page reads, in full: Translator's Preface by Mobi Ho vii; One, The Essential Discipline 1; Two, The Miracle Is to Walk on Earth 11; Three, A Day of Mindfulness 27; Four, The Pebble 33; Five, One Is All, All Is One: The Five Aggregates 45; Six, The Almond Tree in Your Front Yard 55; Seven, Three Wondrous Answers 69; Exercises in Mindfulness 79; Nhat Hanh: Seeing with the Eyes of Compassion by James Forest 101; Selection of Buddhist Sutras 109. The sub-heading 'Washing the dishes to wash the dishes' stands early in the book, after the opening anecdote of Allen and his son Joey, with the running page number 2 just above it and 3 immediately below the proposed sentence. Chapter One runs pp. 1 to 11 and chapter Two begins on p. 11. So the passage is in CHAPTER ONE, 'The Essential Discipline', p. 3, NOT in chapter 2. The evidence says in terms 'The sentence stands in chapter Two under the sub-heading Washing the dishes to wash the dishes', and that is false; the locator field repeats it as ch. 2, 'The Miracle Is to Walk on Earth'. The source line compounds it by printing the sub-heading where the chapter title belongs, so a reader sent to ch. 2 would not find the line. A second problem with the evidence, which is why the error went unnoticed: the URL it names is a GitHub gist of 2,540 bytes, a bare excerpt headed 'Washing the dishes to wash the dishes' with two ellipses in it and no table of contents whatever. The claim to have read 'a full text of the Mobi Ho translation' whose 'table of contents runs One, The Essential Discipline...' is not supported by the source cited; the table of contents was supplied from somewhere else and the chapter was then guessed wrong against it. WHAT HOLDS. The quotation is verbatim in the Beacon text: 'While washing the dishes one should only be washing the dishes, which means that while washing the dishes one should be completely aware of the fact that one is washing the dishes.' It is followed by 'At first glance, that might seem a little silly: why put so much stress on a simple thing?', exactly as the evidence says. shipped.js: no match, no near match, Thich Nhat Hanh at 0 of 3, not banned. Not in the misattribution list, Nhat Hanh's own prose, no speaker question. In scope: 1974 in Vietnamese, Mobi Ho's English of 1976, not scripture or liturgy but a practice manual written as a long letter to Brother Quang, nothing needing a warning. Tag Philosophy is acceptable. Perfect for stillness and attention. Fix the locator and it ships.
